questions.q: What is the holy book of Muslims called?
questions.info: The Quran is the final divine book revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

questions.q: What is the first surah of the Quran?
questions.info: Al-Fatiha comes first in the written Quran.

questions.q: How many daily prayers are obligatory?
questions.info: There are five: dawn, noon, afternoon, sunset and night.

questions.q: Which prophet built an ark by Allah's command before the great flood?
questions.info: Noah built the ark by Allah's command; the believers survived the flood.

questions.q: Which prophet was saved after praying inside a fish?
questions.info: Jonah prayed to Allah inside the fish and was saved (Al-Anbiya 87–88).

questions.q: Which prophet was thrown into a fire that did not burn him?
questions.info: Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Abraham (Al-Anbiya 69).

questions.q: For which prophet did the sea part when he struck it with his staff?
questions.info: Moses and the Israelites crossed the parted sea and escaped Pharaoh.

questions.q: Which prophet was thrown into a well by his brothers?
questions.info: Joseph's story is told in Surah Yusuf.

questions.q: Which act of worship is obligatory in Ramadan?
questions.info: Fasting in Ramadan is obligatory for every healthy Muslim who has reached puberty.

questions.q: Who was the first human and the first prophet?
questions.info: Adam was both the first human and the first prophet.

questions.q: In which city was Prophet Muhammad born?
questions.info: Muhammad (peace be upon him) was born in Mecca. Sources give 570 or 571 CE as his birth year.

questions.q: In which city is the Kaaba?
questions.info: The Kaaba stands within the Sacred Mosque in Mecca.

questions.q: What is the purification performed before prayer called?
questions.info: Ablution is required for prayer; when water is unavailable, dry ablution is performed.

questions.q: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's mother?
questions.info: His mother was Amina; she died when he was six years old.

questions.q: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's father?
questions.info: His father Abdullah died before the Prophet was born.

questions.q: Which angel brought Quranic verses to the Prophet?
questions.info: Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, is the angel of revelation.

questions.q: What is done for Allah's sake at Eid al-Adha?
questions.info: Muslims who can afford it sacrifice an animal at Eid al-Adha.

questions.q: What do we say when beginning a task?
questions.info: The basmala means: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

questions.q: How do Muslims greet one another?
questions.info: The greeting wishes peace upon the other person; the reply is Wa alaykum as-salam.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT show good character?
questions.info: The Prophet commanded truthfulness and warned against lying.

questions.q: What is a kind thing to do when a neighbour is ill?
options: Visit and ask how they are
questions.info: Visiting the sick is one of the rights Muslims have over one another.

questions.q: To which city did the Prophet migrate from Mecca?
questions.info: The migration from Mecca to Medina took place in 622 CE.

questions.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
questions.info: The Quran contains 114 surahs.

questions.q: Which animal did Solomon hear speaking in the Quran, making him smile?
questions.info: This is related in Surah An-Naml, The Ant (18–19).

questions.q: Which book was revealed to David?
questions.info: The Psalms were given to David, the Torah to Moses and the Gospel to Jesus.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Torah revealed?
questions.info: The Torah is the book revealed to Moses.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Gospel revealed?
questions.info: The Gospel is the book revealed to Jesus.

questions.q: Why is the adhan recited?
options: To announce the end of Ramadan
questions.info: The adhan calls people to prayer at each prayer time.

questions.q: Which prophet was born without a father?
questions.info: Jesus was born to Mary without a father.

questions.q: Who was the Prophet's daughter and Ali's wife?
questions.info: Fatima was the mother of Hasan and Husayn.

questions.q: Who was the Prophet's first wife?
questions.info: Khadija was also the first person to accept Islam.

questions.q: In which cave did the Prophet receive the first revelation?
questions.info: The first revelation came in Hira Cave on the Mountain of Light.

questions.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.info: They are the testimony of faith, prayer, fasting, zakat and pilgrimage.

questions.q: How many articles of faith are there?
questions.info: Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and divine decree.

questions.q: What is help given to someone in need for Allah's sake called?
questions.info: Sadaqah is kindness done for Allah's sake without expecting anything in return.

questions.q: What do we say after eating to give thanks?
questions.info: Alhamdulillah means: Praise be to Allah.

questions.q: Which title meaning trustworthy was given to the Prophet in his youth?
questions.info: The people of Mecca called him Al-Amin because of his honesty.

questions.q: On which day of the week is the Friday prayer performed?
questions.info: The Friday prayer is performed in congregation at noon on Friday.

questions.q: Which prophet was Joseph's father?
questions.info: Jacob was Joseph's father.

questions.q: Which son built the Kaaba with Abraham?
questions.info: Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the Kaaba (Al-Baqara 127).

questions.q: In which year CE did the migration from Mecca to Medina take place?
questions.info: The migration was in 622; the Hijri calendar takes this event as its starting point.

questions.q: In which year after the migration was the Battle of Badr?
questions.info: The Battle of Badr was in 2 AH (624 CE).

questions.q: In which year after the migration was the Battle of Uhud?
questions.info: The Battle of Uhud was in 3 AH (625 CE).

questions.q: In which year after the migration was Mecca conquered?
questions.info: Mecca was conquered in 8 AH (630 CE).

questions.q: Who was the first caliph after the Prophet?
questions.info: The four caliphs were, in order, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali.

questions.q: Who was the second caliph?
questions.info: Umar became caliph after Abu Bakr.

questions.q: Under which caliph were Quranic verses first collected into one volume?
questions.info: They were collected after the Battle of Yamama under Abu Bakr; copies were made under Uthman.

questions.q: Under which caliph were copies of the Quran sent to major centres?
questions.info: Copies were produced and sent to Islamic centres under Uthman.

questions.q: In which year did the Prophet die?
questions.info: The Prophet died in Medina in 632 CE.

questions.q: What is the longest surah of the Quran?
questions.info: Al-Baqara has 286 verses and is the longest surah.

questions.q: What is the shortest surah of the Quran?
questions.info: Al-Kawthar has three short verses and is the shortest surah.

questions.q: In which surah is Ayat al-Kursi?
questions.info: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Al-Baqara.

questions.q: Who was Islam's first muezzin?
questions.info: Bilal al-Habashi was the companion with a beautiful voice who first called the adhan.

questions.q: Towards what was the Muslim prayer direction changed from Jerusalem?
questions.info: About 16–17 months after the migration, the prayer direction changed to the Kaaba (Al-Baqara 144).

questions.q: What is the zakat rate on money and trading goods?
questions.info: Money and trading goods reaching the nisab threshold are subject to zakat of one fortieth.

questions.q: In which Hijri month is the hajj performed?
questions.info: Hajj takes place on specific days of Dhu al-Hijja.

questions.q: Which month of the Hijri calendar is Ramadan?
questions.info: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Hijri year.

questions.q: When is dry ablution performed?
options: When water is unavailable or unusable
questions.info: Dry ablution replaces ablution when water is unavailable or cannot be used.

questions.q: How many obligatory acts of ablution are there in the Hanafi school?
questions.info: Wash the face, wash the arms including elbows, wipe a quarter of the head and wash the feet including ankles.

questions.q: How many obligatory units are in the dawn prayer?
questions.info: The dawn prayer has two obligatory units.

questions.q: How many obligatory units are in the sunset prayer?
questions.info: The sunset prayer has three obligatory units.

questions.q: Which grandfather cared for the Prophet as a child?
questions.info: After his mother died, Abd al-Muttalib cared for him; after his death, his uncle Abu Talib did.

questions.q: Which uncle protected the Prophet for many years?
questions.info: Abu Talib also protected him from the polytheists during the early years of his prophethood.

questions.q: On which night did the revelation of the Quran begin?
questions.info: Surah Al-Qadr states that the Quran was revealed on the Night of Decree.

questions.q: Which mosque did the Prophet first build as he approached Medina?
questions.info: Quba Mosque was built during the migration before entering Medina.

questions.q: In which year after the migration was the Treaty of Hudaybiyya signed?
questions.info: The Treaty of Hudaybiyya was signed in 6 AH (628 CE).

questions.q: What are the Muslims of Medina called?
questions.info: Ansar means helpers; those who migrated from Mecca are called Muhajirun.

questions.q: Who was the Prophet's wet nurse?
questions.info: Halima as-Sadiyya nursed and raised the Prophet in the desert as a child.

questions.q: To which mosque was the Prophet taken from the Sacred Mosque during the Isra?
questions.info: The first verse of Surah Al-Isra describes this night.

questions.q: Who is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran?
questions.info: Mary is named explicitly in the Quran; a surah also bears her name.

questions.q: Who commanded the army that tried to destroy the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant?
questions.info: This event is described in Surah Al-Fil; it occurred in the year of the Prophet's birth.

questions.q: Which surah tells the story of the Companions of the Cave?
questions.info: Their story is in Surah Al-Kahf.

questions.q: In which cave did the Prophet and Abu Bakr hide during the migration?
questions.info: They stayed in Thawr Cave for three days.

questions.q: Which title given to Umar means one who distinguishes truth from falsehood?
questions.info: Abu Bakr is called As-Siddiq and Uthman Dhun-Nurayn.

questions.q: Into how many juz sections is the Quran divided?
questions.info: The Quran is divided into 30 juz; communal readings often follow these sections.

questions.q: In which month is the tarawih prayer performed?
questions.info: Tarawih is prayed after the night prayer during Ramadan.

questions.q: In which country did Joseph become an administrator?
questions.info: Joseph was put in charge of the storehouses in Egypt.

questions.q: Which brother of Moses was also a prophet?
questions.info: Aaron was sent to help Moses.

questions.q: By when should zakat al-fitr be given?
questions.info: The Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed that it be given before people go to the Eid prayer. Companions also gave it one or two days earlier.

questions.q: How many circuits are made around the Kaaba in tawaf?
questions.info: Tawaf consists of seven circuits around the Kaaba.

questions.q: At the beginning of which surah are the first revealed verses?
questions.info: They are the first five verses of Al-Alaq, beginning with the command to read in the name of the Creator.

questions.q: Which revelation scribe led the collection of the Quran under Abu Bakr?
questions.info: Zayd ibn Thabit was a revelation scribe and led the collection.

questions.q: Who is the imam of the Hanafi school?
questions.info: Abu Hanifa (died 767) lived in Kufa; the Hanafi school of law is widespread in Turkey.

questions.q: Who wrote the famous hadith collection Al-Jami as-Sahih?
questions.info: Sahih al-Bukhari is considered one of the most reliable hadith sources.

questions.q: Which Muslim mathematician is regarded as the founder of algebra?
questions.info: The word algebra comes from Al-Khwarizmi's work Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala.

questions.q: Who wrote the medical work The Canon of Medicine?
questions.info: This work was used as a medical textbook in Europe for centuries.

questions.q: Which mosque did architect Sinan call his masterpiece?
questions.info: Selimiye in Edirne is his masterpiece; Suleymaniye his journeyman work and Sehzade his apprentice work.

questions.q: Which mosque did architect Sinan call his apprentice work?
questions.info: Sehzade Mosque in Istanbul is Sinan's apprentice work.

questions.q: Which Umayyad caliph commissioned the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
questions.info: The Dome of the Rock was completed in 691–692 CE.

questions.q: In which city was the Abbasid centre of learning, the House of Wisdom?
questions.info: Many works were translated into Arabic and scholarly research took place there.

questions.q: Which work by Ibn Khaldun is famous for its philosophy of history?
questions.info: The Muqaddimah is a pioneering work on society and history.

questions.q: Who wrote the Book of Optics on light and vision?
questions.info: Ibn al-Haytham was a pioneer of optics.

questions.q: In which year was the Battle of Manzikert?
questions.info: The Seljuks under Sultan Alp Arslan defeated Byzantium, opening the way into Anatolia.

questions.q: Under which sultan did the caliphate pass to the Ottomans?
questions.info: The caliphate passed to the Ottomans after the Egyptian campaign of 1517.

questions.q: Which theological school is widespread in Turkey?
questions.info: The two major Sunni theological schools are Maturidism and Asharism; Maturidism is widespread in Turkey.

questions.q: Which caliph introduced the Hijri calendar?
questions.info: Under Umar, the year of the migration was adopted as the calendar's starting point.

questions.q: Where did the Prophet mainly deliver the Farewell Sermon during his final hajj?
questions.info: During the Farewell Hajj (10 AH), he addressed people in the valley at Arafat, declaring the inviolability of life and property. He also gave a sermon on the day of Eid.

questions.q: Which surah lists the eight categories eligible for zakat?
questions.info: They are listed in verse 60 of Surah At-Tawba.

questions.q: What is the status of the witr prayer in the Hanafi school?
questions.info: Hanafis consider witr wajib; other schools consider it sunnah.

questions.q: What is the prostration at the end of prayer for certain mistakes called?
questions.info: Sahw means forgetfulness or error.

questions.q: For a non-traveller, how long is wiping over leather socks permitted?
questions.info: The period is 24 hours for a resident and three days and nights for a traveller.

questions.q: Who wrote the Masnavi?
questions.info: The Masnavi was written in Persian and contains about 26,000 couplets.

questions.q: Who wrote Kutadgu Bilig?
questions.info: Kutadgu Bilig is a work on governance written in the Karakhanid period.

questions.q: Which Karakhanid ruler was the first to become Muslim?
questions.info: The Karakhanids accepted Islam with the conversion of Satuq Bughra Khan.

questions.q: What is the black cloth covering the Kaaba called?
questions.info: The kiswa is renewed each year.

questions.q: How many obligatory elements does hajj have in the Hanafi school?
questions.info: Ihram is a prerequisite; standing at Arafat and the visitation tawaf are pillars. The Prophet said that hajj is Arafat.

questions.q: Which surah does not begin with the basmala?
questions.info: Surah At-Tawba begins without the basmala.

questions.q: Which surah contains the basmala twice?
questions.info: It appears at the start of Surah An-Naml and in verse 30.

questions.q: Which surah is known as Umm al-Kitab, Mother of the Book?
questions.info: Umm al-Kitab is one of the names of Al-Fatiha.

questions.q: Which companion suggested digging a trench around Medina in the Battle of the Trench?
questions.info: This defensive method was known in Persia; Salman al-Farisi suggested it.

questions.q: Which companion, known as Master of Martyrs, was killed at Uhud?
questions.info: The Prophet's uncle Hamza was martyred at Uhud.

questions.q: Which famous Andalusian mosque is in present-day Spain?
questions.info: Construction of the Great Mosque of Cordoba began in the eighth century.

questions.q: In which year did Mehmed II conquer Istanbul?
questions.info: Istanbul was conquered on 29 May 1453.

questions.q: In which city did Sunni theologian Abu Mansur al-Maturidi live?
questions.info: Al-Maturidi lived and died in Samarkand (died 944).

questions.q: Which mosque contains the Prophet's tomb?
questions.info: The Prophet's Mosque is in Medina.

questions.q: Which title given to Khalid ibn al-Walid means Sword of Allah?
questions.info: The Prophet gave him the title Sayfullah.

questions.q: Which title given to Ali means Lion of Allah?
questions.info: Ali is also called Haydar.

questions.q: What were hospitals called in Islamic civilisation?
questions.info: Bimaristans, also called dar al-shifa, were institutions where the sick were treated.

questions.q: What were the famous madrasas founded by Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk called?
questions.info: The Nizamiyya madrasas were founded in the eleventh century in Baghdad and many other cities.

questions.q: Which prophet whose story is in the Quran is known for patience?
questions.info: Job is an example of patience despite serious illness and loss (Sad 44).
